title: Management API
description: Inspect, retry, pause, and delete jobs and queues programmatically

blocks.text: HoundManagement provides a programmatic interface to inspect and control jobs and queues. It uses the same storage backend as Hound and can be used standalone or alongside a running instance.
The simplest path is to read it off a HoundApp — one constructor wires the worker, the management API, and a typed defineJob:

import { HoundApp } from 'hound/';

const { hound, management } = new HoundApp({ db: redis });
Or instantiate HoundManagement directly when you only need the admin surface (e.g. a CLI script that talks to a remote Hound's storage but does not run handlers):

import { HoundManagement } from 'hound/';

const management = new HoundManagement({ db: redis });

Upgrading a deployment with pre-existing job data? Run management.api.reindex() once (or POST /management/reindex) — it rebuilds the indexes from a one-time keyspace scan. Everything written afterwards indexes itself automatically.

rows: List jobs, filtered by queue or status; paginate with limit and offset
Remove a job and all its state keys
Fire a delayed or waiting job immediately
Freeze a job by pushing its delay to max

blocks.text:
// Page 3 of failed jobs, 20 per page (sorted newest first)
await management.api.jobs.find({ status: 'failed', limit: 20, offset: 40 });

Reads are index-backed: find() and stats() consult per-queue sorted-set indexes maintained by the engine, and only the requested page’s payloads are fetched — no keyspace scans, regardless of how many jobs exist.

Destructive: flush all jobs and state from the queue
Returns true if the queue is currently active

blocks.text: reset() is destructive and irreversible. It removes all jobs in the queue including completed and failed records.

Events are in-process by default — the worker that ran the job fires them. Pass a Broker to HoundApp to receive events from jobs that completed in other processes; see the Broker page.
